cases.query: Analyze the trace for binder-related I/O blocking and explain the evidence-backed root cause.
goldenPoints: Identify the binder path and the blocking I/O interval from trace evidence.
Separate the observed wait from unsupported causal speculation.

cases.query: Analyze the framework pipeline execution and identify the stage that dominates latency.
goldenPoints: Reconstruct the pipeline stage order from trace evidence.
Attribute the dominant delay to a concrete stage and time range.

cases.query: Produce a general performance diagnosis while preserving evidence and identity contracts.
goldenPoints: State only conclusions supported by trace evidence.
Preserve process and thread identity when describing findings.

cases.query: Analyze GPU workload timing and determine whether GPU execution is the primary bottleneck.
goldenPoints: Quantify relevant GPU work intervals.
Distinguish GPU saturation from CPU-side submission delay.

cases.query: Trace the input interaction path and explain the main contributor to end-to-end latency.
goldenPoints: Anchor the interaction start and visible response in the trace.
Identify the largest latency segment without conflating adjacent work.

cases.query: Analyze Linux system state and explain the most important scheduling or resource constraint.
goldenPoints: Use system-state evidence to identify the constrained resource.
Relate scheduling state to the affected workload with correct identities.

cases.query: Analyze window-animation smoothness and continuous main-thread work in the constructed interval from the start of SmartPerfetto::CASE::main-thread-frame-work to the end of SmartPerfetto::END::main-thread-frame-work. Scope the investigation to com.smartperfetto.fixture, com.smartperfetto.unframed, and com.smartperfetto.unlabeled. Identify observed tasks, scheduling states, and task-origin locators inside and outside doFrame; explain what the trace does and does not establish about delayed frames, then give appropriately conditional recommendations.
goldenPoints: For com.smartperfetto.fixture, identify ContentLoader$MainHandler: initializeContent as 30 ms between doFrames, with 28 ms Running and 2 ms Runnable; locate the nested parseContentModel 14 ms and inflateContentViews 8 ms without adding child time to parent time or treating labels as proven implementation.
Identify bindRemainingContent as 40 ms between doFrames, including 30 ms Running and 10 ms D-state waiting; D-state alone does not prove file I/O, Binder, or a named blocker.

Report three observed doFrames of 22, 24, and 8 ms, with start intervals of 52 and 68 ms; distinguish observed execution spacing from requested deadlines, presentation cadence, refresh rate, and proved missed frames.

For com.smartperfetto.unframed, identify 40 ms of initializeWithoutFrameMarker work with no doFrame marker; for com.smartperfetto.unlabeled, identify 35 ms of unannotated Running. Missing frame or slice markers do not prove no work or no rendering request.

Preserve the full marker-bounded window, process/UPID/UTID and task slice/state/time locators, separate Running from Runnable/waits/unknown, and disclose sampling and source-origin limitations without importing unrelated base-trace frame counts.

Treat concurrent content work as an observed occupancy and candidate interference mechanism, not a proven deadline miss. Recommend moving parsing/computation only after verifying implementation and dependencies; keep required UI work on the main thread and consider splitting, batching, or deferment.

cases.query: Analyze the media, network, and camera pipeline and identify the evidence-backed bottleneck.
goldenPoints: Reconstruct the relevant cross-component media path.
Attribute delay to a measured component rather than temporal proximity alone.

cases.query: Analyze memory and garbage-collection pressure and explain its performance impact.
goldenPoints: Quantify garbage-collection or allocation pressure from trace evidence.
Connect pauses to workload impact without overstating causality.

cases.query: Analyze power and thermal behavior and determine whether throttling affects the workload.
goldenPoints: Identify thermal or frequency changes in the relevant time window.
Distinguish correlation from evidence of throttling impact.

cases.query: Analyze rendering jank and identify the dominant cause of missed frames.
goldenPoints: Quantify missed or delayed frames in the interaction window.
Attribute jank to a concrete CPU, GPU, or scheduling interval.

cases.query: Reconstruct user input, device state and application response over the trace. Preserve exact observations, unknowns and independent object identities.
goldenPoints: Distinguish physical input from dispatch recipients, touch movement from confirmed scrolling, and ACTION_SCROLL from a physical wheel.
Preserve the observed CANCEL and exact input endpoints; gaps remain unobserved rather than idle.
Retain leading unknown screen and charging states and raw DeviceState values 17 and 23 without inferring unlock, posture or a transition at the first sample.
Preserve raw Scroll and FlingStart marker timestamps and process identities; marker-name duration does not prove an observed action endpoint.

cases.query: Analyze scheduler and CPU contention and identify the workload most responsible for delay.
goldenPoints: Quantify runnable or blocked time for the affected thread.
Resolve the competing process or thread identity from evidence.

cases.query: Diagnose the startup mechanism, separate trace facts from source explanation, and identify the exact source location, call chain, and actionable seam.
goldenPoints: Treat the trace marker occurrence and duration as trace-authoritative facts; a CodeRef alone cannot prove that the event occurred.
Identify StartupHooks.initializeOnMainThread in StartupHooks.kt with the exact generated line and call chain.

Map the trace marker to the source mechanism established by the exact authorized read and recommend the bounded post-first-frame seam; owner-facing quotations are allowed with relative source references, while credentials, private canaries, registered absolute roots, and private-knowledge material outside the authorized inputs remain excluded.

cases.query: Analyze application startup and explain the dominant lifecycle bottleneck.
goldenPoints: Bound the startup interval with trace evidence.
Identify the lifecycle stage that contributes the largest measured delay.

cases.query: Analyze the exact SmartPerfetto::CASE::system-scheduling-evidence marker interval for com.smartperfetto.fixture/main. Explain the clipped Running, R, R+, and D state distribution, observed preemption handoff and wakeup evidence, and distinguish raw priority from unknown scheduling policy. Preserve missing frequency and topology evidence rather than inferring CPU classes or a causal competitor.
goldenPoints: Bind the target UPID/UTID and exact marker window; preserve raw boundaries while reporting the independently constructed clipped state totals.
Distinguish R from R+, require the actual same-UCPU successor for handoff evidence, and do not equate successor duration with target delay.
Retain pure-waiting tasks and unknown topology, frequency, policy, and blocked-function evidence; raw priorities alone do not prove RT/FIFO/RR.

cases.query: Who applied the CPU frequency limit, what was the system running before it, and which threads look anomalous?
goldenPoints: Read the applied limit from the typed cpufreq limit tracks as debounced episodes, never from the actual frequency alone.
Attribute the kernel-thermal episode to the coincident cooling-device transition and keep the daemon-only episode a candidate, not a confirmed thermal cause.
Separate the target app's pre-limit CPU work from system and kernel actors before recommending anything.

cases.query: Compare the Java heap dumps of com.smartperfetto.fixture in this trace: which classes grew between the first and the last dump, and what retains them?
goldenPoints: Compare the first and last heap dump per class on reachable instance counts and dominated bytes from the class aggregation, not on the total heap size.
Name the application class whose reachable instances grew across every dump as the leak candidate, and treat the growing byte[] and Object[] as its retained payload.
Report the holder whose instance count stayed flat while its retained set grew as the likely retention point, and keep the leak a candidate until a reference path confirms it.

cases.query: Why was the main thread of com.smartperfetto.fixture blocked on a lock, and which thread held it for how long?
goldenPoints: Tie the main-thread monitor contention to the owning thread and the method it held the lock in.
Read the holder's lock_held interval as one merged hold that ends when the waiter acquires the lock, not as the sum of its nested slices.
Separate the one contended hold from the short uncontended holds instead of treating every hold as blocking.

cases.query: How long did com.smartperfetto.fixture and its :sync process spend in each framework process state, and what state were they in at the end of the trace?
goldenPoints: Report per-state residency from the framework process-state data, keeping it separate from oom_score_adj.
Follow the app from TOP through LAST_ACTIVITY into CACHED_ACTIVITY with the OomAdjuster reasons for each change.
State that the :sync process ended the trace in CACHED_EMPTY without inventing a kill or LMK event the trace does not contain.

cases.query: What kept com.smartperfetto.fixture active in the background: app wakelocks, its standby bucket, or freezer state?
goldenPoints: Attribute the app wakelocks by uid and tag and keep them separate from kernel wakeup sources.
Explain the standby bucket move from ACTIVE to RARE as the quota context for deferred background work.
Report the frozen interval and its binder unfreeze reason from a single freezer source instead of adding the statsd and slice records.
